definitions.explanation: The direction considered auspicious for a given year, determined by the Chinese zodiac. Traditionally, facing this direction while performing certain activities was believed to bring good fortune. In modern Japan, most commonly associated with the Setsubun custom of eating ehōmaki (lucky direction sushi roll).

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}の{恵方|えほう}は{南南東|なんなんとう}だ。
examples.english: This year's lucky direction is south-southeast.

examples.japanese: {恵方|えほう}{巻|ま}きを{恵方|えほう}を{向|む}いて{食|た}べる。
examples.english: Eat the ehōmaki while facing the lucky direction.

examples.japanese: {節分|せつぶん}の{日|ひ}に、{家族|かぞく}みんなで{恵方|えほう}を{向|む}いて{無言|むごん}で{恵方|えほう}{巻|ま}きを{食|た}べるのが{我|わ}が{家|や}の{習慣|しゅうかん}だ。
examples.english: On Setsubun, it's our family's custom to face the lucky direction and eat ehōmaki in silence.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly encountered in the compound {恵方|えほう}{巻|ま}き (ehōmaki), a sushi roll eaten on {節分|せつぶん} (February 3). The custom involves eating the entire roll in silence while facing the year's lucky direction. The lucky direction changes each year according to the Chinese zodiac cycle.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {恵方|えほう}{巻|ま}き: ehōmaki (lucky direction sushi roll)
- {恵方|えほう}を{向|む}く: to face the lucky direction
- {恵方|えほう}{参|まい}り: visiting a shrine in the lucky direction
- {今年|ことし}の{恵方|えほう}: this year's lucky direction

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {恵方|えほう}{巻|ま}き tradition originated in the Kansai region and spread nationwide through convenience store marketing in the late 1990s and 2000s. It has become one of the most commercially successful seasonal food customs in Japan.
